support_anna: Customer reported 5/6 targets unhealthy behind their ALB in Private. App returning intermittent 502s and ALB health checks show TLS handshake failures. Escalating, need networking/infra eyes.

eng_oncall_jordan: On it. Can you paste the ALB health check config + a couple of ALB access_log lines showing the failure?

support_anna: Pasting health check snippet and log lines:
```
Protocol: HTTPS
Port: 8443
Path: /health
Host header: 10.0.20.15
Matcher: 200-399
Interval: 30s
```
ALB log entry: `2026-03-17T09:12:04Z target:10.0.20.15:8443 TLS_alert handshake_failure`

netops_li: Quick checks: (1) ALB HTTPS health checks use the Host header as the SNI value during TLS handshake. If Host is an IP, SNI will be the IP — many backends/Envoy filter chains reject that. (2) Ensure target SG allows inbound from the ALB SG (not just IP ranges). (3) If the backend cert only includes svc.acme.internal, SNI must match.

support_anna: Customer had locked their Envoy to require SNI `svc.acme.internal`. Their health check Host was the IP, so SNI=IP and handshake fails. Their VPC egress allowlist was also very strict, but that affects outbound from instances (not ALB->target) — still worth flagging.

eng_oncall_jordan: Two viable fixes:
- Update ALB health check Host header to `svc.acme.internal` so SNI matches the cert.
- Or switch health check to plain HTTP on a non-TLS endpoint (if they can accept reduced checks).

Second, advice on firewall: best practice is to allow traffic from the ALB via SG references on targets rather than trying to maintain AWS ELB IP lists. If they must use IP allowlists, remind them ELB health-check IPs can vary.

support_anna: I ran a repro from our bastion to emulate ALB SNI/Host behavior:
```bash
curl -vk --resolve 'svc.acme.internal:8443:10.0.20.15' https://svc.acme.internal:8443/health
# -> TLS handshake: success, HTTP 200
```
From ALB logs we saw `tls: handshake failure` which matches SNI mismatch.

netops_li: Also flagged a DNS gotcha: their internal DNS CNAME resolves the service name to the instance IP. ALB health checks reach the IP directly but rely on configured Host header for TLS/SNI. If the cert only lists the DNS name, you must set Host header accordingly.

csm_maya: I messaged the customer with the two options and recommended updating the ALB health check Host header to the internal service name. They said they'll apply the change now.

eng_oncall_jordan: Action items we asked the customer to perform: 1) Change health check Host -> `svc.acme.internal`. 2) If they can't, temporarily switch to HTTP health checks. 3) Ensure target SG references ALB SG, not static IP ranges. 4) Review egress allowlist to ensure internal Route53 resolvers or any required upstream endpoints are reachable.

support_anna: Customer updated the health check Host to `svc.acme.internal`. Targets became healthy within ~90s. Customer confirmed traffic is routing and 502s stopped. Closing the escalation unless they see recurrence. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: update-healthcheck-host -> prod (2026-03-17T10:05:12Z)
